explain.say: A fuse is a deliberately weak link in a circuit. When something goes wrong and too much current flows, it breaks first, on purpose.

explain.say: Current heats any wire, and more current means much more heat. The fuse wire is the thinnest part of the circuit, so it heats up fastest.

explain.say: When the current is too big for its rating, the fuse wire melts and leaves a gap. The loop is broken, and the current stops before the cables get dangerously hot.

faq.a: A fuse blows when more current flows than its rating, for example 6 amps through a 3 amp fuse. That can come from a short circuit, a faulty appliance or too many devices on one supply.
Inside the glass or ceramic tube is a thin wire made to melt at a known current. Many fuses are packed with sand to smother the spark when the wire melts.
asks: What is a fuse made of?

faq.q: Why does a blown fuse stop the current?
faq.a: When the wire melts it leaves a gap, so the circuit is no longer a complete loop. With no path, no current flows, and the cables cannot overheat and start a fire.
asks: How does a melted fuse cut the power?

faq.q: Can I use a bigger fuse instead?
faq.a: No. A fuse rated too high may not blow before the cable overheats, which can cause a fire. Always use the rating the appliance needs, and find out why the old one blew.
asks: What fuse rating should I use?

faq.q: Does a fuse stop you getting a shock?
faq.a: Not really. A fuse protects wiring and appliances from overheating and fire, but it is too slow to save a person from a shock. Homes use RCDs for that.
asks: What does a fuse actually protect?

facts: The heat made in a wire rises with the square of the current, so double the current gives four times the heat.
UK plug fuses usually come in 3, 5 and 13 amp ratings.

quiz.say: Why is the wire inside a fuse made thin?
quiz.show: Why is the wire inside a fuse made thin?

options.show: So it heats and melts first
options.say: So it heats and melts first

quiz.why: A thin wire has more resistance and heats fastest, so it melts before the rest of the circuit gets too hot.

wrong.1: Saving metal is not the point; it must be the weak link.
wrong.2: A thin wire does not speed up the current.
